It has been revealed that a, Datasets were curated and compiled as described in Fig. 1a. The remaining pipeline was run separately and in parallel for mouse and human data. All computation was performed in R. Schematic created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/w8x4pii (2026). b, Quality control metrics included ensuring that the number of unique genes per cell (nFeature_RNA) was > 200 and the fraction of mitochondrial reads was <20%. Cells with nFeature_RNA ≥ 95th percentile were also removed as a precaution against doublets. c, Data were then converted into an optimized read/write disk space using BPCells. d, To further streamline computation, all data were then sketched into representative 1,000-cell subsets on a per-study basis. e, The resulting data (12.8 M cells for human or 2.5 M cells for mouse) were then integrated on a per-study basis using three independent approaches (Harmony, scVI, FastMNN), resulting in three distinct clusterings and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) embeddings. f, Each of the three objects from e were annotated independently in a semi-supervised fashion using canonical markers in conjunction with the automated classification toolkits SingleR and scATOMIC, resulting in seven coarse cell type designations for each of the three distinct objects. g, For each of the six TME cell types (epithelial cells are excluded moving forward), separate and parallel computational pipelines were followed. This begins with pooling all cells designated as a given cell type (e.g., fibroblasts) by any of the three integration approaches, and creating a common object. h, Each cell type-specific object undergoes re-integration using study-specific batch keys, followed by normalization, scaling, principal component analysis (PCA), UMAP, clustering, and re-annotation to assess purity. Improperly classified cells are then removed, and this process of recursive cleaning is repeated until all cells are found to be of the correct cell type. i, Once all cells are found to be correctly classified, the final atlas for that cell type is annotated and final subpopulations are determined. j, As described above, the process from g to i is repeated→ separately for each of the primary six TME cell types in this atlas.

Industry observers note that a, Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) embeddings of 1,000 sketched cells per study integrated using Harmony, scVI, and FastMNN integration techniques. b, UMAP projections of sketched results from each integration approach onto all 12.8 million single cells in the human atlas. Cells are grouped into seven main cell type clusters. c, Dot plots indicating expression levels of characteristic markers for each of the seven cell types. d, Venn diagrams showing overlap in cell annotations among the three integration approaches and the final atlas. e, Ratios of the number of cells in the intersection versus union of Venn diagrams for each cell type in d. Notably, applying the intersection excludes many cells that may be desirable to include in the final atlas. f, Ratio of cells for each type that are included the final atlas compared to those that would have been arrived at by using the intersection of the three integration approaches. Ratios greater than one indicate the presence of cells in our final atlas that would otherwise have been excluded using an intersectional approach. Illustration of the human created in BioRender; Wang, H. https://biorender.com/q41gtvr (2026).

In a recent development, top-left, UMAP projection based on inferred CNV profiles, where individual cells are colored by their global CNV score. Higher scores (yellow) indicate a greater degree of chromosomal aberration, while lower scores (dark blue) represent cells with profiles closer to the diploid reference. Top-right, The same CNV-based UMAP embedding, with cells colored according to our cell type annotations. The spatial clustering indicates that different cell lineages share similar large-scale genomic gains and losses. Bottom, Heatmap of inferred large-scale CNV patterns. Rows are labeled according to our cell type annotations. Columns represent genomic coordinates, with ticks indicating chromosome boundaries. Color corresponds to relative CNV intensity, where red denotes genomic gains and blue denotes genomic losses. CNV inference was performed on a 100,000-cell subset of the human atlas.

Recent findings suggest that a–d, Dot plots displaying the expression of characteristic, subpopulation-defining marker genes for fibroblasts (a), endothelial cells (b), mural cells (c), and nerve cells (d). Dot size represents the percentage of cells within a given subpopulation expressing the indicated gene, and color intensity denotes the average scaled expression level. To further validate the lineage specificity of these annotations, the rightmost columns of each plot display the absence of expression for established marker genes corresponding to alternative parent cell types (designated as non-fibroblast, non-endothelial, non-mural, and non-nerve, respectively).

a–d, UMAP embeddings of the human atlas coloured by per-cell SCENIC regulon activity score, showing higher activity of the RUNX3(+) and IKZF1(+) regulons in apCAFs (a), the ETV7(+) and IRF2(+) regulons in ISG15+ iCAFs (b), the CREB3L1(+) and NKX3-2(+) regulons in mCAFs (c), and the CEBPA(+) and FOXO3(+) regulons in ssCAFs (d). e, Analysis of metabolic programs for all stromal populations using scMetabolism. f–h, Metabolic activity for CAFs (f), endothelial cells (g), and mural cells (h). a–h, Analyses were performed on 100,000-cell subsets of the human atlas. e–h, Dot size and colour denote the scMetabolism pathway activity score for each population.

#60359. Aberdeen's latest manager is a proven overachiever with a major personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1339 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Aberdeen's latest manager is a proven overachiever with a major personality... but can Dons get a bounce from their Super Mario?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:12 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 15:20 EST, 19 November 2026.

Stephen Robinson was probably destined to fail at Aberdeen in any event. While unquestionably a successful manager with Motherwell and St Mirren, there was always a lingering doubt about whether his skill set would work at a bigger club with different expectations in terms of style of play. And so it proved.

What didn’t help the Northern Irishman was the perception that those who employed him weren’t exactly bowled over by him in the first place, either.

Robinson would have been a hard enough sell to the Dons support had he been unveiled a few days after Jimmy Thelin departed the scene in January.

That it took them 67 days to deliver confirmation of the appointment – after the club had dalliances with Eirik Horneland and Sandro Schwarz – was hardly a ringing endorsement of their faith in him.

The contrast with the process to appoint Mario Frick is striking. Robinson was sacked two days after a four-goal home thrashing by Hibernian. Five days later, the former Liechtenstein international was named by the Pittodrie club as the new head coach.

Industry observers note that after the saga at the start of the year which reflected well on no one, Aberdeen, to give them their dues, knew what they wanted and saw Frick as a hand-in-glove fit. So, what led them so quickly to his door?

Mario Frick is unveiled at Pittodrie and immediately vowed to transform the club's fortunes.

The 52-year-old, essentially, is a head coach who fits in with the overarching strategy Aberdeen identified several years ago.

This has been lost along the way as poor results have seen a churn of individuals occupy the dug-out, many of whom were square pegs in round holes. This, the club believe, has been why the recruitment has been so random and ineffective.

There’s been little joined-up thinking, as evidenced by the summer window which saw 15 players arrive, many of whom were sub-standard or clearly not part of Robinson’s proposal.

The intention always was for the head coach to work in tandem with the sporting director and chief executive rather than independently of them.

While Frick will have a say on what players arrive and depart this January, the conversations around the identity of the team and what’s required to improve it will be three-way.

At Luzern, Frick was happy to trust the judgment of director of football Remo Meyer on such matters.

His willingness to forge the same relationship with Aberdeen’s sporting director, Lutz Pfannenstiel, was the light bulb moment for chief executive Adrian Bevington and chairman Dave Cormack.

Frick earned 125 caps for Liechtenstein and scored 16 goals for the European minnows.

In keeping with the much-vaunted ‘continental’ model, Pfannenstiel and head of recruitment Darren Mowbray will largely identify players to fit the system. Frick will then be tasked with making it all work.

The initiative is for the squad to be closely aligned with the head coach’s needs rather than assembling the rag bag of players who’ve come in the three windows since Thelin won the Scottish Cup.

There’s much beyond Frick’s willingness to defer matters of player identification to others which caught the eye of the board, however.

Although very much a modern and forward-thinking coach, he’s vastly experienced in the game.

As a player, he turned out for Swiss clubs including St Gallen, Basel, Zurich and Grasshopper.

He became the first Liechtensteiner to play professionally in Italy with AC Arezzo before signing for Verona, Ternana and Siena.

Across 125 internationals, he became Liechtenstein’s all-time top scorer with 16 goals, including one against Scotland at Hampden in 2010, the infamous game which saw Stephen McManus ride to the rescue with a 90th-minute winner.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington welcomes fresh manager Frick to Pittodrie.

Recent findings suggest that being the star man for an underdog may have had something to do with his upbringing. Frick’s father didn’t exactly encourage him to make it as he started out in the game.

He once revealed in an interview: ‘He told me: ‘There are thousands of talents like you. You won’t make it.’.

His coaching journey began eight years ago with Vaduz, who he succeeded in getting promoted to the Swiss Super League via a play-off.

Appointed head coach of Luzern almost five years ago, he turned the side from relegation candidates into one capable of finishing fourth inside 18 months. There followed finishes of seventh, sixth and seventh place prior to an amicable parting of the ways when his contract expired in May.

Although Frick didn’t win anything, Luzern is not a club which is accustomed to doing so, with their last league title arriving in 1989.

Its supporters still strongly identified with him, though, and recognised that he often got more out of modest resources than he was entitled to.

They enjoyed his big personality – not scared to wind up opponents in the media and not shy at publicly calling out his own players when they didn’t live up to the standards he’d set.

Frick famously scored for Liechtenstein against Scotland in a 2-1 at Hampden in 2010.

When he left there at the end of last season, the supporters felt the loss of a passionate manager who wore his heart on his sleeve, had no time for egos and stopped at nothing to deliver success.

Sources indicate that in the Granite City, he will call out anyone not giving their absolute all every moment they are in a red jersey. And unlike the diplomatic Thelin, the fireworks are likely to be seen in public.

If his time at Luzern proves prescient, those who resist or disrupt the dressing room will soon be moved on. Those who do their best by him will have nothing to fear, however.

As Italian football fan Fabio Baccarini will gladly attest, although tough and demanding, Frick is also renowned as being a loyal man with a huge heart.

Baccarini, from Reggio Emilia, became fascinated by Frick in the early 2000s while collecting Panini stickers due to the fact that he played for Liechtenstein, a tiny nation he struggled to pronounce.

He wrote so many letters to his various clubs, hoping to arrange a meeting, that Frick initially feared he might be a stalker.

When they first met in 2011 after a game between Liechtenstein and San Marino, the forward presented Baccarini with a signed shirt, gave him his email address and invited him to a match in Vaduz.

And so began an extraordinary friendship which saw Baccarini regularly drive 1,000km to support the minnows and become their de facto mascot.

In a recent development, three years back, when Hibs travelled to Luzern in the Conference League, the Italian super-fan was unable to find a bed for the night. Frick ensured he got one in the team hotel at no cost.

The new Pittodrie boss is just the latest to follow in the footsteps of the great Sir Alex Ferguson.

As heartwarming as such tales are, it was, of course, the metrics of on-field success which drew Aberdeen to him.

Frick’s willingness to give young players a chance – another criticism made of Robinson – was a tick against his name.

He’s handed top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career. He appointed Ardon Jashari, who played against Scotland on Monday, his Luzern captain at the age of 20.

It has been revealed that he does not appear to be wedded to a particular formation. He mostly played a 4-4-2 with a diamond at Luzern, but he’s very much a pragmatist.

When he takes his bow at Rugby Park on Saturday, he’ll select a system to suit the personnel rather than trying to shoehorn the players into a pre-ordained system.

With just two points separating their team from bottom-side Kilmarnock, how the Red Army could do with witnessing a Super Mario bounce.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have a lot of decisions to make about their current crop of players.

A decent chunk of their contracts are set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, no extensions have been agreed.

Obviously, the Reds will have certain players who they'd prefer to keep over others but, the decision may not be up to them.

Thanks to how good most of Liverpool's players are, clubs from across the world have shown their interest in acquiring their services which means that the L4 outfit will have a fight on their hands to try and keep most of them.

And, for one player, even though it felt like he was going to be locked down, his future has now been blown back open once again.

The future of Rio Ngumoha is still undecided.

Rio Ngumoha is a player who Liverpool need to keep hold of at any cost.

The young Englishman has been a regular starter for Andoni Iraola and, even though he's not really managed to get off the mark yet, his performances have still been impressive.

People forget that the former Chelsea man is still only 18 years old so, the fact that he's even being chosen to start for Liverpool in the first place is a big thing.

The talent that Ngumoha possesses is obvious to anyone who watches him play so, even though his current contract doesn't expire until 2028, fans can see why Liverpool want to lock him down.

However, a fresh update from Fraser Fletcher has shared a bit more of an insight into what the future has in store for Ngumoha.

"Bayern Munich are very keen on him [Rio Ngumoha],” Fletcher mentioned.

“They have now moved to make him and his representatives aware that they would like to bring him in.

“Of course, Liverpool don’t want to sell such a brilliant young talent in January.

“At just 18 years old he’s already lit up Anfield on a couple of occasions and Andoni Iraola is keen to keep him.

“Liverpool are keen to push him through their development initiative for him and get him tied down to a latest deal.

“No new deal has been signed yet meaning his future is [still] open.”.

Liverpool can't let Bayern Munich sign Rio Ngumoha.

The fact that talk of Ngumoha exiting Liverpool is even making the light of day should be questioned.

The 18-year-old has had a huge impact during his short time as a first-team regular with Thomas Tuchel even calling him up to England's national team.

As mentioned, he may not have found a purple patch of form yet but, from the movements and chances that he creates, you can tell that Liverpool have a gem on their hands.

Bayern Munich are one of the biggest teams in the world and, the fact that they want Ngumoha proves how good he must be.

Harry Kane has just won the Ballon D'Or thanks to his performances for the Bundesliga outfit which demonstrates that they only have elite talent in their ranks.

Obviously, they'd have to pay Liverpool to sign him right now but, it doesn't feel like any sort of fee would be worth them accepting.

Nobody knows how these contract talks are going to go but, if they don't end with the attacker signing a new deal, some serious questions will need to be asked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

It has been revealed that going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the prepares for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a latest destination would be found, but Amorim had other plans. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Sources indicate that such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

In a recent development, “A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”.

“I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”.

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

According to recent reports, “I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”.

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

According to recent reports, “I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”.

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

In a recent development, “It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”.

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

What do you remember about America?

Sources indicate that “Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”.

In a recent development, “I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”.

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

It has been revealed that “Yes, in 2021 I returned to New York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”.

Is it true you have a cat named Bronx?

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”.

Your family moved from America to Italy….

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”.

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

Sources indicate that “Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”.

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”.

You have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

Leeds are making their second trip to Stamford Bridge this season, having already going down 6-3 to Chelsea in a chaotic EFL Cup tie in September.

Despite Chelsea's dominant Stamford Bridge record, Leeds avoided defeat to Chelsea in last season's Premier League.

Leeds head into this fixture having recorded five points from their five away matches in this season's Premier League.

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1,2,3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune–metabolic homeostasis4,5,6,7,8,9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

Real-time voltage output of the NeuroAxis under dynamic glucose concentration changes.

Recent findings suggest that logic control of NeuroAxis during closed-loop glucose-responsive neuromodulation. The NeuroAxis-mediated VNS is triggered only after the glucose level exceeds a threshold of five consecutive readings. Once the stimulation condition is met, the system delivers biphasic electrical pulses for 3 min.

Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working

📅 17 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4306 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly.
  • Recent findings suggest that this has all the makings of a long, hard season.
  • After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

Recent findings suggest that this has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

Industry observers note that this was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

Johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa in front! 🟣 https://t.co/jxZf2568Sl.

According to recent reports, it is getting hard to comprehend what Jaissle wants his team to do. The much-hyped “vertical” style looks like an ugly incarnation of the long ball football of yesteryear. They did not like it at Newcastle in the 1980s and 1990s and some fashions should never return. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

There is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Newcastle are not getting better; they are making all the same mistakes and, if anything, as an attacking force, they are looking increasingly stale and predictable. They did not have a shot on target in the first half and, other than one fantastic save in the second, Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki had nothing to do.

"If he doesn't slip Harvey Barnes in, he's got to hit the target" Shay Given discusses Newcastle's decision-making in the final third 🔲 https://t.co/wh4kCAEbxV.

“Our decision-making in the final third was lacking today,” Jaissle mentioned. “I am frustrated, I understand the supporters’ reaction, that is their right [to boo after a defeat at home].”.

Industry observers note that it is time for a sharp dose of medicine on Tyneside. Expectations need to be adjusted, especially as none of the fresh signings have impressed. This was always the fear and the risk when you put all your faith in young players from abroad.

Recent findings suggest that for Jaissle’s vertical football to work, Newcastle need to be able to win the ball high up the pitch, whether that is with a high press or competing for second balls from long passes. They do not do either well. More worryingly, they look so vulnerable, so easy to play through.

Sources indicate that villa did it to them all afternoon. Nicolas Jackson should have scored in the first half, Ibrahim Mbaye should have hit the target in the second.

On another day, Newcastle could also have had centre-back Sven Botman sent off for a lunge on Jackson. Then it really would have become ugly, but the Dutchman survived a VAR check.

Recent findings suggest that villa were always the better side. There was no fluency in Newcastle’s game, no structure, no patterns of play. Every time they turned over the ball, they looked stretched. Every time they got a set-piece, it was defended easily. Every time they went forward in the first half, the ball was sent aimlessly long and came straight back at them. In the second, they huffed and puffed but did not sustain any pressure on the Villa goal. The missed chances late on were not clear opportunities and they were snatched at by the hapless Yoane Wissa.

Yoane Wissa fails to hit the target after an inspiring run! ❌ https://t.co/ohabzLZBRv.

It was largely poor and so was the manner in which Villa took the lead. João Gomes was given the time and space to loft a cross to the far post for Manzambi, who had drifted away from Lewis Miley, to head home.

Newcastle were in disarray and it should have been 2-0 almost immediately when Emiliano Buendía received the ball in the middle of the area and crashed a shot against a post.

Sources indicate that the home crowd tried to remain patient and supportive, but the sight of yet another long, aimless ball being punted forward straight to a Villa defender tipped some over the edge. There were boos and jeers in the stands while Jaissle screamed at Joe Willock and Wissa. There were more boos at half-time; things felt combustible.

It has been revealed that newcastle needed a big second half. They were better, but it was hardly anything to get excited about. A shot on the turn from Botman, superbly saved by Suzuki. Then a few half-chances were squandered, the occasional flash of a threat and that was it.

"That was too easy" Matthias Jaissle discusses Aston Villa's winner against Newcastle 🗣️ https://t.co/deg1ALxVBR.

"We have a no excuses culture" Tyrone Mings on Aston Villa's significant win against Newcastle 👏 https://t.co/PsrVkdNi3i.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Sky Sports, the Villa man said: “It was a difficult game. St James’ Park is always very difficult to play in. Very happy we got the three points and very happy to win here.”.

When asked about the Botman challenge in the first half, he replied: “The referee mentioned it was a yellow card but it was so high. Hopefully next time it is a red card. I nearly broke my leg, but it’s fine. It’s part of football.”.

100 - Unai Emery recorded his 100th win as a Premier League manager, doing so in his 197th game in the competition, only eight managers have done so in fewer games than the Spaniard. Impressive. https://t.co/Zk7z8rh7u5.

In a recent development, he's in your head. https://t.co/ivjceHI45e.

Villa have done it! They have dug in to secure a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James’ Park, with Manzambi’s first-half header enough to separate the sides. Villa move up to 12th, level on points with Newcastle in 11th, who have now lost three of their last four Premier League games. There’s questions for Jaissle, while Villa are beginning to gather momentum this season under Emery after a slow start.

HEADING HOME WITH THREE POINTS 😍 https://t.co/qIppjjqsvZ.

According to recent reports, A Newcastle cross causes chaos in the Villa box, with Mings heroically hooking the loose ball away. That could do it for Villa, who are seconds away from the three points.

Sources indicate that jackson can’t make the most of the latest Villa break, with Hall and Thiaw defending well. Burn is quite literally playing everywhere, popping in numerous areas across the pitch. Still, a goal eludes Newcastle.

Burn is playing as a makeshift striker. The game has descended into a free-for-all from a Newcastle perspective.

Mbaye goes close again! The winger skips away from Miley and darts into the box, before dragging a low strike narrowly wide of the bottom corner. He’s been so direct and positive since entering the action. Burn is on for Newcastle to replace Joelinton in Jaissle’s final roll of the dice. There’s six minutes of added time for the hosts to find a late leveller.

Our final change as we enter six minutes of stoppage time... HWTL! [0-1] 90' https://t.co/zMj893Ye1W.

Industry observers note that villa are closing in on the three points. They’ve limited Newcastle to very little in forward areas. The victory is within touching distance now for Emery’s side.

Thiaw is booked for lunging in on Mbaye and preventing a Villa attack. Eight yellow cards have now been handed out this evening at St James’ Park, with six going to Newcastle players.

Wissa is wasteful! The striker initially does brilliantly to evade Kamara’s challenge and dribble towards Villa’s box. However, instead of playing in Barnes for an easier strike, Wissa shots, but curls the effort wide. Barnes is furious with his teammate. The frustration from the home fans is very audible.

It has been revealed that yoane Wissa fails to hit the target after an inspiring run! ❌ https://t.co/ohabzLZBRv.

According to recent reports, mbaye misses the chance to seal the victory for Villa! McGinn drives forward, allowing Barkley to play in Mbaye. The winger bursts into the penalty area, and from a tight angle, fires his one-on-one effort over the bar.

Joelinton tees up Wissa, who slices a rushed effort wide of the near post. Wan-Bissaka’s earlier withdrawal sees Mings move out to full back and Pau Torres slot into a central position.

It has been revealed that osula slides in on Pau Torres. It’s a little late and he gets a yellow. It’s a harsh decision. You can see why everyone associated with Newcastle is so incensed by that.

Recent findings suggest that wan-Bissaka pulls up with an injury and is unable to continue. He clutches his right hamstring and trudges off the pitch with the help of two medical staff members. Pau Torres is on as his replacement.

We're forced into a change as Pau comes on for Aaron 🔄 ⚫️ 0-1 🟣 77' #NEWAVL https://t.co/8Eekl7Ndmg.

According to recent reports, newcastle take a page out of Villa’s book, fashioning a dangerous counter. Cash is one-on-one with Osula and the defender times his challenge perfectly to stop the forward from advancing any further.

Recent findings suggest that barkley goes close! Villa fly forward on the break through Jackson, and with his first touch of the game, Barkley arrows a fierce half-volley at goal, only to see Hornicek expertly tip it away.

Lukas Hornicek denies Ross Barkley to keep Newcastle in touching distance 👊 https://t.co/Ltiq2Kbr5X.

Confirmation of that triple substitution as Goretzka, Barkley and Mbaye replace Joao Gomes, Buendia and Manzambi.

A triple change, well played lads 👊 ⚫️ 0-1 🟣 72' #NEWAVL https://t.co/wP54myqtFk.

It has been revealed that manzambi is down and in need of treatment. Gonzalez hurriedly goes over to try and help the Villa man, but Manzambi isn’t interested. A triple change for the visitors is imminent.

It has been revealed that miley’s searching cross is headed away by Lindelof but only as far as Wissa. The former Brentford man attempts an acrobatic volley, only to see it blocked by a couple of Villa bodies.

Sources indicate that villa are retreating deep, inviting Newcastle to put them under some pressure. However, the hosts are lacking attacking invention and threat, with Villa’s lead still looking relatively safe.

Recent findings suggest that miley clips in a cross and Wissa wins the header. The striker directs his looping attempt over the bar. It won’t classify as a chance, but it’s more encouraging from Newcastle.

Wan-Bissaka tracks back excellently to defend against Toure before getting his body in front of the ball to win a foul. It’s another decision met by furious boos from the home fans.

Jaissle orders a double change in forward areas as Osula and Toure replace Fernandez-Pardo and Willock.

Industry observers note that A double switch 🔄 Come on, lads! 💪 [0-1] 57' https://t.co/ysiribFvcI.

Wissa closes down Suzuki and the striker catches the goalkeeper. There’s no malice in challenge, but the Newcastle man is booked. Safe to say that the majority of St James’ Park don’t agree with the decision.

Gonzalez cynically pulls McGinn back as the Villa captain glides away from the Newcastle midfielder, who picks up a yellow card.

That Botman shot was by far the closest Newcastle have come to scoring so far. The home fans will hope they can continue to put Villa under pressure.

Sources indicate that botman tests Suzuki! Villa fail to clear a Newcastle free kick and the ball breaks to Botman, who swivels and powers a first-time effort at goal. The venomous strike forces Suzuki into a brilliant diving save. Botman scored a stunner at Coventry on Monday and saw his names in lights again, but Suzuki was there to deny him.

We are back under way for the second half. Villa have made a half-time alteration, with McGinn replacing Alysson, who was booked in the first half, while Newcastle are unchanged.

Another dreadful half for Newcastle United and the home fans are getting increasingly exasperated with Matthias Jaissle’s tactics. The aimless long balls pumped forward for nobody to reach, and which normally go straight to an Aston Villa defender, have drawn boos. There were more at the half-time whistle. Whatever the blueprint is, it isn’t working and it has not for weeks. A pattern is emerging, and it is really worrying for Newcastle. They look like a disorganised mess.

#NEWAVL – 17' The referee's call of yellow card to Botman for the challenge on Jackson was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "I think it's reckless. Even though you get a touch on the ball, it's still reckless".

Villa have been the better side and deservedly lead Newcastle 1-0 at St James’ Park thanks to Manzambi’s header. The visitors look so dangerous on the break in forward areas, while the hosts are struggling at the back. Botman was also lucky to escape a red card following a VAR review of his forceful challenge on Jackson. Pedro Goncalves has revealed that he once requested to leave Sporting Lisbon for Aston Villa.

Although still contracted to the Primeira Liga giants, Pote at the moment finds himself on loan at Fiorentina.

However, the 28-year-old is already established as a Sporting legend, a result of contributing 97 goals and 66 assists from 239 appearances in all competitions.

Goncalves also has three Portuguese league titles to his name, but in an interview with Record, he has suggested that he wanted his career to take a different path.

Despite having only joined Sporting on a five-year contract in August 2020, Goncalves says that he wanted to accept an offer to join Aston Villa shortly afterwards.

He said: "I only asked to leave once, and that was to manager [Ruben] Amorim.

"I spoke to him directly, but that was a long time ago.".

When pushed on which club he wanted to join, Pote added: "It was right in my first year [2020/21].

It has been revealed that "It was reported in the press. I had an offer from an English club. It was Aston Villa.".

With no further details provided over timings, the assumption is made that Goncalves's chance to join Villa came in the 2021 summer transfer window.

Villa would spend £33m on Emiliano Buendia during that particular period, a player who has since gone on to become one of the club's trusted players under Unai Emery.

Dean Smith was in charge of Villa at the time.

Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Industry observers note that evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

It has been revealed that evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

It has been revealed that whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially confirmed Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

Jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

It has been revealed that during a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

It has been revealed that mike Maignan is expected to start in goal. He took part in a portion of yesterday’s training session alongside the other goalkeepers. It has been revealed that strahinja Pavlovic also participated in part of the group training and will be included in the squad for the match against the Ciociari. However, the Serbian defender is not yet at 100%, so unless his condition improves rapidly, he is likely to start on the bench.

Sankhoun Diawara would thus take the left centre-back spot, with either Davide Bartesaghi or Pervis Estupinan covering the left flank. The defence will be completed by Koni De Winter and Mario Gila, with the Spaniard operating on the right again.

In midfield, Yunus Musah, Luka Modric and Adrian Rabiot – who could play in a more advanced, attacking-midfield role – are expected to be the starting trio. In attack, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos are guaranteed starters, with Christian Pulisic currently favoured over Alphadjo Cisse.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric; Pulisic, Rabiot, Moreira; Ramos.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Birligea.

Industry News: 115 charges distraction? Enzo Maresca addresses Man City’s slump in form and “avoidable” problem

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 17:36.
  • Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has dismissed suggestions that the Premier League financial charges case is affecting his players following a concerning dip in form.
  • In September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 17:36.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has dismissed suggestions that the Premier League financial charges case is affecting his players following a concerning dip in form.

In September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts and bogus deals to disguise more than £830m in secret funding and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case,” and they have subsequently lodged an appeal.

A wide range of potential sanctions have been mooted for Man City should their guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City responded to the bombshell news with a statement 3-0 Premier League win away against Liverpool, but they have since won just four of their last eight games in all competitions (including one in the EFL Cup on penalties).

Maresca’s side entered November’s international break after a disappointing run of three consecutive Premier League defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, losing 3-1 away to the latter a fortnight ago.

The Citizens have conceded 17 goals across their last nine matches and have failed to keep a clean sheet in that time, while some first-team stars have come under fire for making costly errors leading to goals.

Man City currently sit third in the Premier League table, six points behind leaders Arsenal who will welcome the Sky Blues to the Emirates Stadium next week.

Maresca’s players have regularly faced media questions over the ongoing financial charges case, and while the Man City boss accepts that those queries are fair game, he insists the issue is not affecting results on the pitch.

"If you ask, they need to answer and if you ask me I need to answer," Maresca told reporters at a press conference on Friday.

In a recent development, "I'm here to answer, so if you are going to ask the players because they want to be polite they need to give you an answer. If you don't want to talk about that don't ask the players about the noise.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that. If we want to relate the noise with the defeat, Villa away we had so many chances - for instance, Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, Brighton's keeper was Man of the Match, at Forest where Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score [to make it] 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise.".

This comes after former Manchester United defender Gary Neville suggested after City’s loss at Forest that Maresca’s players are being affected by the off-field scandal.

Speaking on NBC Sports, Neville noted: "It's all everybody's talking about back home in the last month or so and those players will be getting asked constantly: 'What do you think is going to happen? What happens if they do get relegated, will you stay?'.

“Imagine that your family is having to put up with that, your agent is continually thinking about those things so it can't be ruled out as a factor that that's going to start to seep in.

"Obviously if you lose a football match or two that's going to start to look like an excuse but they have to play better, compete in games, make sure that they do better from a tactical and physical perspective.

“But I do believe it will be having some impact just because of the weight of what's been hitting them from a publicity point of view in the last four to six weeks.".

Explaining what he believes is the main reason behind Man City’s recent decline, Maresca remarked: "For sure, we are conceding avoidable goals. For instance, the third goal against Forest. They have 11 players inside the box defending and we concede the third goal.

“We reviewed things during the international break that we need to do better, and again, the idea is to continue to attack in the same way, creating chances, and trying to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened with the first goal against Forest, where if we can avoid mistakes, it's always better.".

Maresca now faces an urgent tactical puzzle ahead of Saturday's clash with Fulham, as he bids to fix the glaring midfield imbalance and address the dilemma he has with Enzo Fernandez.

#60340. Industry News: Are you ok, Noni?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1371 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Arseblog ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Are you ok, Noni?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal’s squad construction has given them a lot of depth and diversity in terms of profiles.
  • Havertz and Gyokeres for centre-forward.
  • It has been revealed that on the face of it, Noni Madueke should really be in that third layer of the squad with Mosquera, Kepa and where Zubimendi probably now resides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal’s squad construction has given them a lot of depth and diversity in terms of profiles. Timber and White for right-back, Calafiori and Hincapie for left-back. Ezri Konsa has, incredibly, offered both protection and threat to the impregnable Saliba and Gabriel partnership. Bruno and Lewis Skelly, Rice and Zubimendi and Odegaard and Merino for midfield.

Eze and Tzolis for the left-wing. Havertz and Gyokeres for centre-forward. Of course, some of these pairings are more symbiotic than others. Mosquera is probably going to fall behind Konsa as a back up to either one of Saliba or Gabriel. In reality, Zubimendi is only going to play ahead of Rice if Rice is injured or Arsenal have a nice easy game against League Two opposition, for example….

It has been revealed that on the face of it, Noni Madueke should really be in that third layer of the squad with Mosquera, Kepa and where Zubimendi probably now resides. The role of back-up to Bukayo Saka ought to have been one with limited opportunity. In a sense, I was always a little surprised that Madueke signed up for it when he came to the club from Chelsea last summer.

I was slightly surprised that Arsenal spent so much money on a player who was always incredibly unlikely to dislodge Saka no matter how much he improved. And how much scope was there going to be for Madueke to get the sort of rhythm and consistency of selection to hone his talents?

Recent findings suggest that now I strongly suspect that Arsenal would have had anxieties over Saka’s ability to stay fit after tearing his hamstring in December 2024 and missing a few months of football. It was the first significant injury Saka had incurred and after quickly deciding that loanee winger Raheem Sterling was not going to be an adequate replacement, they amended for his absence with a blend of 17-year-old Ethan Nwaneri and surplus left-back Kieran Tierney.

It isn’t difficult to see how Arsenal viewed the right-wing spot as a single point of failure but encouraging Madueke to see it as an attractive position must have challenged even Mikel Arteta’s powers of persuasion. Yet just over a year on from signing for Arsenal, Madueke has a league title winners medal (‘while others are tweeting and posting’) with 25 starts to his name last season, 16 of which were in the Premier League.

In reality, being Bukayo Saka’s third leg has, to this point, proved to be a savvy career move for Madueke because he is getting plenty of time on the pitch in Saka’s increasing absences. This extends to the England National Team too, where Madueke plays the same role. But it was a role that still earned him four starts for his country in a World Cup, including a start in the quarter-final against Norway.

A Premier League title winners medal, a Champions League Final appearance and four World Cup starts was not a bad return for Madueke in terms of playing time. I think we knew when Arsenal bought him that Noni was a talented but phlegmatic player, relentless in taking on his full-back but the quality of his end-product could vary markedly.

In his new signing profile of Madueke on Arseblog, Phil Costa wrote, ‘there’s a feeling that Arsenal lack penetration from their wingers (Bukayo Saka aside); chaos factor, some unpredictability, and Madueke brings this in spades. His first thought when receiving the ball is centred around provoking defenders and driving towards goal, which means you can isolate him without too much focus on the overall setup – you just wind him up and let him go.

‘There are two specific metrics to love when assessing the 23-year-old; per FBRef data, he at the moment sits in the 95th percentile for progressive carries (6.82 per 90) and the 98th percentile for carries into the box (4.12 per 90). Those are big numbers.’ There was never any doubt about Madueke’s ability to get the ball into threatening areas, the question has always been what he does when he gets there.

Last season, some clips of him harumphing the ball out of the stadium on his right foot went semi-viral. I also think some of his performances were impacted by a lack of balance in the front three. With technicians like Havertz and Odegaard unavailable, he was often playing alongside fellow blunderbusses like Gyokeres and Martinelli.

Sources indicate that I admit that my tolerance for inefficiency is high when it comes to attackers. I think attacking is a volume game. The vast majority of attacks come to nothing, the vast majority of shots do not go in or even work a goalkeeper. Individual attacks are the weather but, overall, attacking is the climate. The more you do it and sustain it, the more likely you are to score.

According to recent reports, so my ‘we can fix him’ gene for slightly wayward wingers is high. I didn’t even mind Gervinho (a frustrating player, no doubt, but the Bradford miss has become the defining image of his Arsenal career which I don’t believe was fully representative of his performances).

The video of Madueke’s right foot ballooning the ball into the upper tier against Kairat last season has been refined. Both his goals this season have been on his right foot, particularly notably against Nottingham Forest where he cut in on his right and unleashed a low and controlled shot. It might have taken a helpful deflection but that’s because he kept the attempt low.

Last season, his right footed efforts were more in danger of colliding with low flying aircraft on their way into orbit. Noni’s goal against Slavia Praha demonstrated his pace in behind. It was the sort of goal and chance Gabriel Martinelli was hoovering up in Europe last season. European games tend to offer more space in behind and with Martinelli gone, Madueke is one of the few Arsenal attackers explosive enough to exploit it.

Indeed, in my view, he ought to have won Arsenal a match winning penalty in Budapest against Paris Saint Germain in May. There are signs of greater maturity and efficiency in his game. According to WhoScored.com his pass success rate in the Premier League last season was 76.2%. This season so far it is 86.3%.

I think he has learned that he does not have to go for the full-back at 100mph every single time he gets the ball and has varied his game. In the Champions League game against Lille, he sent 15 crosses into the penalty area, having sent six into the area in the game before against Leeds. 15 crosses sounds like a lot but it was very clearly under instruction from Mikel Arteta.

It has been revealed that after that Lille game, the manager said of Madueke, ‘I said when you talk about players being ‘clinical’, sometimes that means scoring five in every 100. It’s about generating volume, more actions and getting him into the good positions, because he will decide matches. He had a really massive contribution a few days ago, today he had a contribution in the last final pass as well.’.

Being omitted from the England squad in September, according to Arteta, provided additional motivation for Noni, ‘After the break, he is showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well as in his actions and he is becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’.

He has now been omitted from the England squad again for the November international round. It is a decision I don’t really understand from Thomas Tuchel but I am happy if it continues to provide Madueke with an additional reason to fine tune his game and because it hopefully protects a player who has become very important.

I admit I am not entirely sure how good Madueke is going to be in, say, three years’ time. He is 24 and it’s at that age that attackers typically start to increase their decisive actions. He has Max Dowman in the rearview mirror too. I think Madueke has a really high ceiling and there are small, but encouraging, signs of improvement.

"We work for Barcelona and want what's best for the club - to win, to build the best possible squad - but we are also humans and we also want to build relationships. They would also have to negotiate with him -- it's not just about paying the clause -- but we would be happy for several reasons [if the deal goes through]. "Firstly, because the move has worked out and because Ronald is happy and is able to continue his career successfully. We want players to succeed. Also, the money would not hurt, either." Based on those words it's a confirmation that Barcelona are happy for Liverpool to proceed with a permanent transfer for Araujo. Whether Ward decides to activate the agreement remains to be seen. But Araujo being his first transfer looks very likely at this stage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

It has been revealed that the result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Recent findings suggest that spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

In a recent development, napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Industry observers note that sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win key for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR.

Sources indicate that it was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

Serie A overtakes Premier League in stunning goalscoring turnaround – what has changed?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 17:38.
  • Serie A has overtaken the Premier League as Europe's second-highest-scoring major domestic competition this season, completing a remarkable transformation from the lowest-scoring of the continent's top five leagues just a year ago.
  • After 110 matches in the 2026-27 campaign, Italy's top flight has produced 342 goals, an average of 3.11 per game, compared with the Premier League's 273 goals in 100 fixtures, or 2.73 per match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 17:38.

Serie A has overtaken the Premier League as Europe's second-highest-scoring major domestic competition this season, completing a remarkable transformation from the lowest-scoring of the continent's top five leagues just a year ago.

After 110 matches in the 2026-27 campaign, Italy's top flight has produced 342 goals, an average of 3.11 per game, compared with the Premier League's 273 goals in 100 fixtures, or 2.73 per match.

Only the Bundesliga, averaging 3.48 goals, presently ranks higher among Europe's five major leagues, with Ligue 1 and La Liga also recording better scoring rates than the English top flight.

The change is particularly striking when measured against the previous campaign.

Serie A averaged just 2.43 goals across the entirety of 2025-26, meaning its current scoring rate represents an increase of approximately 28%.

However, the transformation becomes even more dramatic when comparing the opening 110 matches of both seasons.

Industry observers note that at the same stage last year, Italian clubs had managed just 2.22 goals per game. The latest figures therefore represent a rise of around 40%, raising questions about what has changed in a championship historically associated with defensive organisation.

The difference between the two seasons extends well beyond the overall number of goals.

According to figures compiled by Futbor, only two of Serie A's opening 110 matches this season have ended goalless, compared with 17 at the equivalent stage of 2025-26.

Meanwhile, 21 matches have produced at least five goals, and 60% of fixtures have featured three or more.

The Premier League has reached that three-goal threshold in just 47% of its opening 100 matches.

Italy's attacking revival has also been driven by several clubs rather than one exceptionally prolific team.

Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma lead the scoring charts with 31 goals in 11 matches, followed by defending champions Inter Milan with 28.

Lazio have contributed 25, while promoted Frosinone have scored 24, making them one of the most entertaining sides outside the traditional Italian elite.

The dramatic shift has produced several extraordinary results.

Inter defeated Udinese 5-3 in September, Atalanta drew 4-4 with Frosinone in October, and Lazio recorded a 6-2 away victory over Sassuolo later that month.

Roma also demonstrated their attacking strength with a 5-2 win at Udinese, reflecting the ambitious approach Gasperini has continued to develop since leaving Atalanta.

The contrast with English football is notable.

Arsenal right now lead the Premier League despite scoring only 15 goals in their first 10 matches, relying heavily on a defence that has conceded just five.

The Gunners' consistency illustrates that attacking productivity is not necessarily the determining factor in a successful championship campaign.

Nevertheless, the figures challenge the familiar perception that English football provides greater attacking entertainment than its Italian counterpart.

They also suggest that the recent transformation in Serie A deserves closer examination.

One explanation lies in the growing influence of coaches willing to adopt more aggressive approaches.

Gasperini has long been associated with intense man-to-man pressing, attacking wing-backs and a willingness to commit several players forward.

His influence, established during his successful spell at Atalanta, is now evident at Roma, who have become the division's most productive attacking side.

Cesc Fabregas has brought a different philosophy to Como.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder has built his team around possession, positional rotations and combinations designed to create numerical superiority in midfield.

Although Como's 18 goals in 11 matches fall below the league's most prolific sides, their approach demonstrates the variety of tactical ideas gaining ground in Italian football.

Cristian Chivu represents another example of the changing coaching landscape.

The former Chelsea defender guided Inter to the Serie A title in his first full season in charge and has continued to develop an attack-oriented approach with the reigning champions.

There is also evidence that these changes extend beyond the most recognisable managers.

Massimiliano Alvini's Frosinone have scored more than twice per match, despite operating with significantly fewer resources than Italy's biggest clubs.

Speaking to Italian newspaper Il Foglio, tactical analyst Adriano Bacconi reported that the number of attacking moves ending inside the opposition penalty area had increased by more than 20% compared with the previous season.

That figure offers a potential explanation for the scoring surge: teams are reaching dangerous areas more frequently, increasing the opportunities to create chances.

The greater emphasis on pressing and attacking numbers can also leave defences exposed during transitions.

Former AC Milan defender Filippo Galli suggested that changes in coaching philosophies have contributed to the increase, while acknowledging that modern defenders face increasingly complex responsibilities when building attacks from the back.

Those tactical developments do not mean that Italy's defensive traditions have disappeared.

Indeed, some of the additional goals may reflect defensive vulnerabilities rather than improved attacking quality alone.

The emergence of younger players offers another encouraging development.

Official Serie A figures showed that under-21 players had contributed 49 goals during the opening 10 matchdays, more than in any of Europe's other four major leagues.

Players such as Como's Nico Paz are benefiting from opportunities to assume significant attacking responsibilities, although the development of young talent does not automatically resolve the wider structural problems facing Italian football.

Financially, Serie A remains some distance behind the Premier League, and Italy's failure to qualify for three consecutive World Cups underlines the challenges facing the national game.

The early scoring figures also require perspective: 110 matches represent less than a third of the season, and the average could decline as the campaign progresses.

For now, however, the evidence is compelling.

Serie A has gone from averaging barely more than two goals per match at this stage last season to challenging the Bundesliga for European scoring supremacy.

Its revival suggests that Italian clubs are finding new ways to compete and entertain, even without the Premier League's financial resources.
